[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Equalize the Array** [CF 1490F · Equalize the Array](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1490/F){rating="1500"}

Only the frequencies matter, never the values: count each value, then forget the values and sort the list of counts. For a target count $C$, every value with fewer than $C$ copies is deleted completely and every other value is trimmed to $C$, so you **keep** $C \times (\text{number of values with count} \ge C)$. After sorting the counts $f_0 \le \dots \le f_{m-1}$, the values with count at least $f_i$ are exactly positions $i \dots m-1$, so trying $C = f_i$ costs $O(1)$ and the answer is $n - \max_i f_i \cdot (m - i)$. Sorting on a derived key (the count) turns "how many are at least $C$" into a position.

[Solved in full in @sec-srt-p4-b.]{.card-link}

:::
